nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 8
nodes.statement: We fix an arbitrary $\omega \in \Omega_T$, which is omitted from the notation for brevity. It follows from Proposition \ref{prop: definition of Omega_T} that $q_n(i)$, $\mathcal{A}_n(i)$ and $\mathcal{D}_n(i)$ are identically zero for all large enough $n$ and all $i > B_T' \vcentcolon= B_T + \Delta$\footnote{If $B_T' = B_T$, a task can be sent to a server pool with $B_T$ tasks and at the same instant a task can leave from the same server pool, although this has probability zero; here $q_n(B_T + 1)$ remains zero but $\mathcal{A}_n(B_T + 1)$ and $\mathcal{D}_n(B_T + 1)$ have a jump. Setting $B_T' = B_T + \Delta$ precludes arrivals to server pools with $B_T'$ tasks since $\ell_n \leq B_T$.}. Consequently, we have \begin{align*} u_n(t) = \sum_{i = 1}^{B_T'} q_n(t, i) &= u_n(0) + \sum_{i = 1}^{B_T'} \left[\mathcal{A}_n(t, i) - \mathcal{D}_n(t, i)\right] \\ &= u_n(0) + \frac{1}{n}\mathcal{N}_n^\lambda(t) - \sum_{i = 1}^{B_T'} \mathcal{D}_n(t, i) \end{align*} for all $t \in [0, T]$ and all large enough $n$. To prove the proposition, it suffices to establish that every increasing sequence of natural numbers has a subsequence $\mathcal{K}$ such that $\set{u_k}{k \in \mathcal{K}}$ converges uniformly over $[0, T]$ to $u$. For this purpose, we first observe that \eqref{seq: convergence of initial conditions 2} and \eqref{seq: fslln for arrivals 2} imply that \begin{equation*} \lim_{n \to \infty} u_n(0) = u(0) \quad \text{and} \quad \lim_{n \to \infty} \sup_{t \in [0, T]} \left|\frac{1}{n}\mathcal{N}_n^\lambda(t) - \int_0^t \lambda(s)ds\right| = 0. \end{equation*} Given an increasing sequence of natural numbers, Proposition \ref{prop: relative compactness of occupancy state sample paths} implies that there exist some subsequence $\mathcal{K}$ and a function $q \in D_{\mathbbm{R}^{\mathbbm{N}}}[0, T]$, such that $\set{q_k}{k \in \mathcal{K}}$ converges to $q$ with respect to $\varrho$; note that $q(i)$ is identically zero for all $i > B_T'$. If we define $\tilde{u} \vcentcolon= \sum_{i = 1}^{B_T'} q(i)$, then $\set{u_k}{k \in \mathcal{K}}$ converges to $\tilde{u}$ uniformly over $[0, T]$, and \eqref{seq: fslln for departures 2} yields \begin{align*} &\lim_{k \to \infty} \sup_{t \in [0, T]} \left|\sum_{i = 1}^{B_T'} \mathcal{D}_k(t, i) - \int_0^t \mu \tilde{u}(s)ds\right| = \\ &\lim_{k \to \infty} \sup_{t \in [0, T]} \left|\sum_{i = 1}^{B_T'} \left[\mathcal{D}_k(t, i) - \int_0^t \mu i \left[q(s, i) - q(s, i + 1)\right]ds\right]\right| = 0. \end{align*} We conclude that $\map{\tilde{u}}{[0, T]}{[0, \infty)}$ satisfies the integral equation \begin{equation*} \tilde{u}(t) = u(0) + \int_0^t \left[\lambda(s) - \mu\tilde{u}(s)\right]ds \quad \text{for all} \quad t \in [0, T]. \end{equation*} The unique solution to this integral equation is $u$. Therefore, the sequence $\set{u_n}{n \geq 1}$ converges uniformly over $[0, T]$ to $u$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 15
nodes.statement: It suffices to establish that there exists $k \in \mathbbm{N}$ such that $u_n(t) < (k + 1)\Delta$ for all $t \in [0, T]$ and all sufficiently large $n$. Specifically, if $u_n(t) < (k + 1) \Delta$, then it follows from \eqref{seq: threshold coxian case} that $\ell_n(t) \leq k\Delta$, and clearly $q_n(t, (k + 1)\Delta) < 1$. In particular, incoming tasks are never sent to server pools with $(k + 1) \Delta$ tasks or more during $[0, T]$. Also, recall from Section \ref{sec: notation and assumptions} that $q_n(0, B + 1) = 0$ for all $n$ with probability one, so we can take $B_T = \max \{B, (k + 1)\Delta\}$. Therefore, it is enough to show that \begin{equation*} \bigcap_{m \geq 1} \bigcup_{n \geq m} \set{\omega \in \Omega}{u_n(\omega, t) \geq M\ \text{for some}\ t \in [0, T]} \end{equation*} has probability zero for some $M \in \mathbbm{N}$. Consider the sets \begin{equation*} E_n^M \vcentcolon= \set{\omega \in \Omega}{u_n(\omega, t) \geq M\ \text{for some}\ t \in [0, T]}. \end{equation*} By the Borel-Cantelli lemma, it suffices to prove that there exists $M \in \mathbbm{N}$ such that \begin{equation} \sum_{n = 1}^\infty \mathbbm{P}\left(E_n^M\right) < \infty. \end{equation} The total number of tasks in the system at time $t$ is upper bounded by $\mathcal{N}_n^\lambda(t) + nu_n(0)$, the number of arrivals during $[0, t]$ plus the initial number of tasks in the system. Hence, \begin{align*} \mathbbm{P}\left(E_n^M\right) &\leq \mathbbm{P} \left(\mathcal{N}_n^\lambda(t) + nu_n(0) \geq nM \ \text{for some} \ t \in [0, T]\right) \\ &\leq \mathbbm{P} \left(\mathcal{N}_n^\lambda(t) + n B \geq nM \ \text{for some} \ t \in [0, T]\right) = \mathbbm{P} \left(\mathcal{N}_n^\lambda(T) \geq n\left(M - B\right) \right). \end{align*} The second inequality follows from $q_n(0, B + 1) = 0$, which implies that $u_n(0) \leq B$. Applying a Chernoff bound, we conclude that \begin{align*} \mathbbm{P}\left(E_n^M\right) \leq \mathbbm{P}\left(\mathcal{N}_n^\lambda(T) \geq n(M - B) \right) \leq \frac{\mathrm{e}^{\lambda T \left(\mathrm{e} - 1\right)n}}{\mathrm{e}^{(M - B)n}} = \mathrm{e}^{\left[\lambda T(\mathrm{e} - 1) + B - M\right]n}. \end{align*} Therefore, \eqref{eq: borel-cantelli condition coxian case} holds for any $M > \lambda T (\mathrm{e} - 1) + B$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the threshold through $u_n$, then Borel-Cantelli with a Chernoff bound on total arrivals.

nodes.name: Borel-Cantelli condition (Coxian)
